text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures headed into the weekend in good spirits, shored up by upbeat U.S. Treasuries and a slightly stronger mark. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.75, up 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts continued the week's uptrend to reach 114-24/32 before sheding their gains to settle near the day's low. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 114-02/32, up 06/32 from Thursday's settlement price.
FRANCE - Bond futures settle higher but off best levels in thin volume. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.74 up 0.22 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures showed pared gains in late afternoon reflecting the fall back in U.S. Treasuries with the lira also slipping back against the German mark. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.25 up 0.27 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stayed up, but off day's highs in late morning. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-31/32, up 05/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.91 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply down on Friday, after falling to a seven-month low earlier in the day, due to massive selling triggered by fears of higher interest rates. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.29, up 0.14 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market remained subdued on Friday morning with many European players still absent from their desks after yesterday's holiday. The main exception was a 200 million stg 10-year deal from British television company Carlton Communications, its debut in the Euromarket. Final pricing was due later at a spread of 65 basis points over the key 2006 gilt via lead manager BZW.
Sources close to the issue said while it was an opportunistic financing it was, nevertheless, "a boringly routine transaction".
